summary.text: Jared Moskowitz is the Democratic incumbent, seeking re-election in the renumbered 25th District after Florida's 2026 redistricting. A Broward County native and attorney, he held local office in Parkland, served in the Florida House from 2012 to 2019, led the Florida Division of Emergency Management under Gov. Ron DeSantis, and has been in Congress since 2023. His campaign website describes a record of "action, bipartisan leadership, and crisis-tested experience."

paragraphs.text: Moskowitz was born in Coral Springs, Florida. According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Broward County and graduated from Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from George Washington University (2003) and a law degree from Nova Southeastern University (2007).
He worked as an attorney and political staffer, and as general counsel for AshBritt Inc.
Moskowitz was elected to the Parkland City Commission while in law school and served from 2006 to 2012.

He then served in the Florida House of Representatives, District 97, from 2012 to 2019. His official biography says that after the 2018 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School he worked on the school's Public Safety Act.

In 2019 Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed him Florida's director of emergency management, with responsibility for state disaster recovery, including the response to Hurricane Michael and the COVID-19 pandemic, according to his official biography.
He later served on the Broward County Commission before his election to Congress.
Moskowitz was elected to the U.S. House in 2022, succeeding Debbie Wasserman Schultz in the 23rd District, and was re-elected in 2024.
His official biography lists service on the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs committees.
